I have reported this to Apple because this kind of payment experience is not acceptable. What makes it worse is that the app itself is getting worse every year. versions.name: Critical paywall and billing trust restoration
versions.rationale: Findings F-01, F-02, and F-05 all relate to monetization trust and access: loss of free access, unexpected billing, and deceptive practices. They share subscription/payment implementation scope and have the highest combined user impact, with F-01 alone supported by 11 reviews. Grouping them allows a focused release to restore free access and billing transparency.

versions.name: Reversing AI-generated content quality decline
versions.rationale: Finding F-06 has medium confidence and support (5 reviews), indicating a distinct issue of content quality degradation from AI-generated workouts and avatars. This requires separate implementation work in the content pipeline and is prioritized before lower-impact ad issues.

versions.name: Reducing intrusive ad interruptions
versions.rationale: Finding F-03, while lower support (3 reviews) and low confidence, still represents a recurring user pain point with ads disrupting workouts. It is scheduled as a separate lower-priority milestone because its implementation scope (ad integration and exit flows) differs from subscription/content fixes.

requirements.title: Restore free access to basic workouts
requirements.problem: Users report that the app used to offer free workouts but now most or all features are locked behind a paywall, preventing access to basic exercises without payment.
requirements.user_need: I want to access a set of basic workouts for free so that I can stay fit without being forced into a subscription.
requirements.description: Provide a clearly defined free tier with a meaningful set of basic workouts accessible without payment or payment information. Ensure previously free content is not locked behind a subscription and clearly separate free vs. premium content in the UI.
acceptance_criteria: A user without a subscription can access at least one full basic workout without entering payment information.
The paywall is not displayed before starting or completing a basic free workout.
The workout library clearly indicates which items are free and which require premium.
No previously free workout is moved to premium without an equivalent free alternative.
assumptions: Consumers expect at least some free basic workouts; if this conflicts with business strategy, the free tier must be validated with user research.

requirements.title: Transparent billing and easy cancellation
requirements.problem: Reviews report unexpected charges after free trials, confusing pricing, difficulty canceling subscriptions, and no cancellation reminders.
requirements.user_need: I want clear pricing and an easy way to cancel so that I am not charged unexpectedly and feel in control of my subscription.
requirements.description: Improve subscription flows to show trial terms, renewal price, and cancellation deadline before purchase. Provide an in-app cancellation path and pre-renewal reminders.
acceptance_criteria: Before a user starts a free trial, the UI displays trial duration, price after trial, and cancellation deadline.
A user can cancel their subscription from within the app in no more than 3 steps.
No further charges occur after a user successfully cancels; confirmation is shown and emailed.
A reminder notification is sent at least 24 hours before a free trial converts to a paid subscription.
assumptions: Low review volume; assumed that billing complaints are representative of a broader user base. Requires validation via support tickets and chargeback data.

requirements.title: Eliminate deceptive free and trial claims
requirements.problem: Users feel misled by free access or free trial claims that are not honored; content labeled free requires payment or charges occur immediately.
requirements.user_need: I want marketing and in-app labels to accurately reflect what is free and what is paid so that I do not feel tricked.
requirements.description: Audit all user-facing claims related to free access and trial offers. Ensure any content labeled 'free' is accessible without payment, and trial offers clearly state billing terms.
acceptance_criteria: All content labeled 'free' in marketing or in-app is accessible without entering payment information.
Marketing and trial offers are audited and match actual access and billing behavior.
No charge occurs immediately after a user selects a free trial without an explicit consent step that discloses the charge.
Any reported deceptive claim is corrected within one release cycle.
assumptions: Low evidence volume; assumes the issue is inconsistent labeling rather than intentional deception. A full compliance audit is recommended.

requirements.title: Reverse AI-generated content quality decline
requirements.problem: Reviews criticize the use of AI for workouts and avatars, saying the app has lost its original quality and feels generic or worse after updates.
requirements.user_need: I want high-quality, non-generic workout content so that the app continues to meet my fitness expectations.
requirements.description: Remove or clearly label AI-generated workouts and avatars. Restore and promote original, human-created workout content, and provide a filter or separate channel for users who prefer non-AI content.
acceptance_criteria: AI-generated workout avatars and scripts are either removed or explicitly labeled as AI-generated.
A filter or channel is available for users to select non-AI workout content only.
User satisfaction score for workout content returns to the pre-AI-update baseline within 3 months.
assumptions: Assumes AI-generated content is perceived as lower quality by a significant subset of users; further content audit and user research needed to identify specific quality gaps.

requirements.title: Reduce intrusive ad interruptions
requirements.problem: Users complain about ads that interrupt workouts, are impossible to exit, or open external websites unexpectedly.
requirements.user_need: I want ads that do not disrupt my workout and that I can easily close so that I can focus on exercise.
requirements.description: Rework ad placement and behavior so ads do not interrupt active workout sessions, all ad units have a working close control, and external navigation is only triggered by explicit user action.
acceptance_criteria: No ad is displayed during an active workout session.
All ad units include a visible close button that exits the ad within 2 seconds.
No ad opens an external website or app store without the user tapping the ad's call-to-action.
Ad-related complaints in support and reviews decrease by at least 50% after release.
assumptions: Low evidence volume; assumes ad behavior is an unintended bug rather than a deliberate ad strategy. Requires analysis of ad implementation and user session logs.

requirements.title: Restore free access to basic workouts
requirements.problem: Users report that the app used to offer free workouts but now most or all features are locked behind a paywall, preventing access to basic exercises without payment.
requirements.user_need: I want to access a set of basic workouts for free so that I can stay fit without being forced into a subscription.
requirements.description: Provide a clearly defined free tier with a meaningful set of basic workouts accessible without payment or payment information. Ensure previously free content is not locked behind a subscription and clearly separate free vs. premium content in the UI.
acceptance_criteria: A user without a subscription can access at least one full basic workout without entering payment information.
The paywall is not displayed before starting or completing a basic free workout.
The workout library clearly indicates which items are free and which require premium.
No previously free workout is moved to premium without an equivalent free alternative.
assumptions: Consumers expect at least some free basic workouts; if this conflicts with business strategy, the free tier must be validated with user research.

requirements.title: Transparent billing and easy cancellation
requirements.problem: Reviews report unexpected charges after free trials, confusing pricing, difficulty canceling subscriptions, and no cancellation reminders.
requirements.user_need: I want clear pricing and an easy way to cancel so that I am not charged unexpectedly and feel in control of my subscription.
requirements.description: Improve subscription flows to show trial terms, renewal price, and cancellation deadline before purchase. Provide an in-app cancellation path and pre-renewal reminders.
acceptance_criteria: Before a user starts a free trial, the UI displays trial duration, price after trial, and cancellation deadline.
A user can cancel their subscription from within the app in no more than 3 steps.
No further charges occur after a user successfully cancels; confirmation is shown and emailed.
A reminder notification is sent at least 24 hours before a free trial converts to a paid subscription.
assumptions: Low review volume; assumed that billing complaints are representative of a broader user base. Requires validation via support tickets and chargeback data.

requirements.title: Eliminate deceptive free and trial claims
requirements.problem: Users feel misled by free access or free trial claims that are not honored; content labeled free requires payment or charges occur immediately.
requirements.user_need: I want marketing and in-app labels to accurately reflect what is free and what is paid so that I do not feel tricked.
requirements.description: Audit all user-facing claims related to free access and trial offers. Ensure any content labeled 'free' is accessible without payment, and trial offers clearly state billing terms.
acceptance_criteria: All content labeled 'free' in marketing or in-app is accessible without entering payment information.
Marketing and trial offers are audited and match actual access and billing behavior.
No charge occurs immediately after a user selects a free trial without an explicit consent step that discloses the charge.
Any reported deceptive claim is corrected within one release cycle.
assumptions: Low evidence volume; assumes the issue is inconsistent labeling rather than intentional deception. A full compliance audit is recommended.

requirements.title: Reverse AI-generated content quality decline
requirements.problem: Reviews criticize the use of AI for workouts and avatars, saying the app has lost its original quality and feels generic or worse after updates.
requirements.user_need: I want high-quality, non-generic workout content so that the app continues to meet my fitness expectations.
requirements.description: Remove or clearly label AI-generated workouts and avatars. Restore and promote original, human-created workout content, and provide a filter or separate channel for users who prefer non-AI content.
acceptance_criteria: AI-generated workout avatars and scripts are either removed or explicitly labeled as AI-generated.
A filter or channel is available for users to select non-AI workout content only.
User satisfaction score for workout content returns to the pre-AI-update baseline within 3 months.
assumptions: Assumes AI-generated content is perceived as lower quality by a significant subset of users; further content audit and user research needed to identify specific quality gaps.

requirements.title: Reduce intrusive ad interruptions
requirements.problem: Users complain about ads that interrupt workouts, are impossible to exit, or open external websites unexpectedly.
requirements.user_need: I want ads that do not disrupt my workout and that I can easily close so that I can focus on exercise.
requirements.description: Rework ad placement and behavior so ads do not interrupt active workout sessions, all ad units have a working close control, and external navigation is only triggered by explicit user action.
acceptance_criteria: No ad is displayed during an active workout session.
All ad units include a visible close button that exits the ad within 2 seconds.
No ad opens an external website or app store without the user tapping the ad's call-to-action.
Ad-related complaints in support and reviews decrease by at least 50% after release.
assumptions: Low evidence volume; assumes ad behavior is an unintended bug rather than a deliberate ad strategy. Requires analysis of ad implementation and user session logs.
